item.title: Rattlesnake Lodge Hike — Fri Oct 2, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0 Meet at the Ox Creek Trailhead at 9 a.m. We tend to park at the 2nd and third turn off, once you turn left onto Ox Creek from the Parkway.
We'll leave for the hike at 9:10 a.m. This hike is very rocky, so it's hard on the footing. Most of the hike to the ruins of the lodge is a slight upgrade and, on the return, there is a long stretch of incline just before the hike ends. When it's wet it can be slippery.
Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among already experienced hikers. We repeat the same trails weekly so that, over time, we enjoy the beauty of each trail. We limit our hikes to two hours because many of us work and have to be somewhere else by 11:15 or so. Thus, it's not possible to wait for slower hikers. We shuttle, so if someone is slower, the group would have to wait in order to give a ride back to the starting point. Thus, the need to be on the same page with regard to hiking pace.

item.description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS) Local government decisions shape nearly every part of life in Asheville, from housing and transportation to economic development, public safety, parks, and the future of downtown. Understanding how those decisions are made, and where residents can have a meaningful voice, is not always as straightforward.
Join the AYPROS Government Relations Crew for our October meeting as we continue creating a place where young professionals can better understand local government, discuss the issues affecting our region, and become more informed and involved in the future of Asheville and Buncombe County.
This month, we are pleased to welcome **Asheville City Mayor Esther Manheimer and City Councilor and Mayoral Candidate Kim Roney.**
Members will have an opportunity to hear directly from both, ask questions, and contribute their own perspectives to the conversation.

item.title: Bull Creek Preserve + Swannanoa River Trails — Mon Oct 5, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group We'll start at the Bull Creek Preserve, across the street from Berea Baptist Church. Will do a half loop, counter clock-wise, to the Bull Creek trail, then down the Dam Pasture trail to the Swannanoa River trails. We'll hike to where the trail falls into a creek on the Warren Wilson campus and have our snack at the lower campus. Then it's a return on the river trails after which we'll complete the loop in the Bull Creek Preserve. Distance is appprox. 8 miles, little elevation.
No dogs.
**Parking:** Bull Creek Preserve **ACROSS THE STREET** from Berea Baptist Church, 2578 Riceville Road. Parking is limited so number of hikers is limited.

item.description:

item.description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS) ### **NEW TIME: 8:30–10:00 AM**
Start your Thursday with AYPROS at Flour in downtown Asheville. If Pub Club is your after-work hangout, Mug Club is the morning version. Coffee instead of cocktails, a little caffeine before the workday, and the same easy chance to catch up with familiar faces and meet other young professionals from across Asheville.
##### **And heads up: Mug Club is starting a little later! Beginning this month, we’re moving from 8:00–10:00 AM to 8:30–10:00 AM.**
For October, we’re headed downtown to Flour, a locally owned café on Wall Street serving coffee alongside scratch-made breakfast, biscuits and fresh-baked pastries. Come for the coffee, stay for the company, and maybe let a biscuit talk you into breakfast.
Mug Club is intentionally casual. Leave your business cards at home, come as you are, grab a coffee and settle in for a little while. No program. No presentations. No awkward agenda. Just good coffee and good people

item.title: 9:15 Contemplative Service — Sun Oct 11, 9:15 AM — *1 Sanctuary
item.description:
At 9:15 AM, we have a 40-45 minute Contemplative Worship Service. This service invites participants into a reflective, more meditative space, and includes silence, beautiful recorded music and videos, and opportunities for sharing. It also features the sermon and theme which will be the focus in the second service at 11:15 AM. This service is not livestreamed., and it include childcare but not a full religious education program. This service will be particularly good if you need quiet in order to hear well or focus, would prefer a little more space around you, or seek a more contemplative communal experience. Between services, at 10 am we will have coffee hour and special programs. Whether you come to the early service or the later service, we encourage you to consider arriving at 10 am for coffee, conversation, and special programs including conversations with the Board, or Minister & lay-led justice or adult education offerings.
Source: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Ashevi

item.description:
oin students and faculty to learn about Inside-Out, the College’s higher education in prison program in partnership with Western Correctional Center for Women. Inside-Out is the only program in North Carolina that brings together college students (“Outside”) with incarcerated students (“Inside”) for credit‑bearing courses taught inside the prison.
At this information session, you’ll hear about the courses being offered in Spring Semester 2027, learn how the program works, and listen to first‑hand experiences from students who have participated in Inside-Out classrooms. You’ll also have a chance to ask questions and explore how Inside-Out connects to social justice learning, community engagement, and equity through higher education in prison.

item.title: HERB OPEN CABIN — Wed Nov 4, 4:00 PM — Herb Cabin
item.description:
Herb Open Cabin is every wednesday 4-6pm, come swing by and work with and learn about herbs!!
September 30th- Herb harvesting and processing party!
October 7th- Plant walk/herb garden educational chat!
October 14th- Fall break-
October 21st- Intro to herbal medicine making- making Fire cider!
October 28th- Samhain celebration with herbs!
November 4th- Root Harvesting!

item.title: Belegarth Foam Fighting — Wed Nov 4, 6:00 PM — Cowpie Lawn
item.description:
Fighters, to the field!
The Medieval guild hosts weekly full contact foam fighting on cowpie lawn. Including foam swords, shields, javelins and arrows.
Loaner weapons are provided for everyone for free, and anyone is welcome to come fight and learn!
We play games like capture the flag, or do drills to train fighting skillz.
bring ya friends, bring water, have fun.
Source: Warren Wilson College
